candidates.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
candidates.abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

candidates.title: Systematic study of the performance of small robots on controlled laboratory substrates
candidates.abstract: The design of robots able to locomote effectively over a diversity of terrain requires detailed ground interaction models; unfortunately such models are lacking due to the complicated response of real world substrates which can yield and flow in response to loading. To advance our understanding of the relevant modeling and design issues, we conduct a comparative study of the performance of DASH and RoACH, two small, biologically inspired, six legged, lightweight (10 cm, 20 g) robots fabricated using the smart composite microstructure (SCM) process. We systematically examine performance of both robots on rigid and flowing substrates. Varying both ground properties and limb stride frequency, we investigate average speed, mean mechanical power and cost of transport, and stability. We find that robot performance and stability is sensitive to the physics of ground interaction: on hard ground kinetic energy must be managed to prevent yaw, pitch, and roll instability to maintain high performance, while on sand the fluidizing interaction leads to increased cost of transport and lower running speeds. candidates.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
candidates.abstract: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points. We prove that the sign of each passive eigenvalue equals the sign of the extinct species' density in the enlarged community, that every partial community containing $X_1$ is a saddle with one unstable direction for each extinct consumer, and that the coexistence state is the only stable fixed point. A WKB treatment of the master equation gives a $2N$-dimensional Hamiltonian whose fluctuational fixed points are obtained in closed form. candidates.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
candidates.comment: main: 9 pages, 2 figures, 1 table, supplemental material: 21 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables
candidates.abstract: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.

candidates.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
candidates.comment: 11 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026). Code: https://github.com/soot-bit/pinnslicer
candidates.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. We present PINN-Slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = G(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. A single PINN, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using Sobol-sampled initial conditions. The PINN is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. We demonstrate PINN-Slicer on the nonlinear equation that describes photon orbits around a black hole, and reach a point-by-point root-mean-square error (RMSE) below $10^{-3}$ in $u = r_s/r$ (the inverse radial coordinate in units of the Schwarzschild radius) relative to a finite-difference reference solution. A key advantage of PINN-Slicer is that a single trained network generalizes to any orbital initial condition within the training range, without retraining. candidates.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
candidates.abstract: In many canonical biophysical and biochemical contexts, complex diffusing DNA-binding proteins undergoing nonspecific adsorption and desorption can exist in different conformational states. Equilibrium binding theories and kinetic models of competing ligands provide a basis for describing these systems. Coupling the internal conformational kinetics of bound proteins to exclusion and diffusion requires tracking both protein positions and binding states. Closed-form, tractable mathematical models that accurately describe the stochastic dynamics of structured proteins that bind to and diffuse along DNA are lacking. Here, we develop a new coarse-grained stochastic model of nonspecific DNA-protein binding in the fast diffusion regime, from which we derive an effective Markov model and its corresponding mean-field approximation that incorporates protein footprint size and conformational switching. We fit our new model quantitatively to previously measured dynamics of Replication Protein A (RPA) binding to ssDNA. candidates.comment: 29 pages, 12 figures, ade with generative AI assistance. No clue what the right archive listing for it should be
candidates.abstract: We develop a dynamical phase theory of hierarchy, in which depth decides whether a population of size $N$ that revises its own environment can correct it without overcorrecting. The statistics that let a large majority detect a small bias - the basis of the Condorcet jury theorem - also make its response grow as $\sqrt{N}$. Fed back into the environment it is judging, this sharpening destabilises the matched state through a flip bifurcation at a critical loop gain, which we obtain analytically for a class of models we term adaptive normal forms. We show that this instability can be attenuated by hierarchical layering, requiring a depth scaling logarithmically with $N$. This recovers known logarithmic bounds in organisational economics directly from dynamic stability conditions. Hierarchical depth carries its own costs however, and by analysing the signal chain transmission up the hierarchy we show that beyond a finite depth no correction reaches the top before its deadline, and that below it the cost of arrival grows exponentially with depth. candidates.title: Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE): A Mission Concept for a Low-Frequency Radio Interferometer on the Lunar Farside
candidates.abstract: The universe below 20 MHz remains one of space science's last unexplored frontiers, inaccessible from Earth due to its ionosphere and terrestrial radio frequency interference (RFI). We present the mission concept for the Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE), an all-sky imaging, low-frequency radio telescope operating from 100 kHz-30 MHz from the lunar farside, the quietest radio environment in the inner Solar System. If realized, MoonRISE would be the first radio interferometer on the Moon and the first connected-element radio interferometer in space. Its science objectives are to (1) determine how solar wind turbulence drives plasma heating, acceleration, and space weather evolution in the inner heliosphere, by measuring the scattering of type III solar radio bursts between 2-20 solar radii; (2) constrain the density, structure, and variability of the lunar ionosphere and its effects on surface communication; and (3) resolve the plasma sources and magnetospheric dynamics that power Uranian Kilometric Radiation, observable for the first time since Voyager 2 in 1986. candidates.title: Quantum Noise-Limited Terahertz Interferometry for Distinguishing Ultra-Compact Supermassive Galactic Objects
candidates.abstract: The images of the galactic centers, M87$^*$ and Sgr~A$^*$, obtained by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) provide hitherto unknown revelations on these supermassive objects. The key issue here is the presence or otherwise of an event horizon at these ultra-compact entities. We show here that distinguishing the central images generated by gravitational lensing of a Schwarzschild black hole and a Joshi--Malafarina--Narayan (JMN-1) central naked singularity provides important insights into the nature of these supermassive objects and would help test the cosmic censorship conjecture, central to black hole physics. For optically thin spherical accretion onto Sgr~A$^*$, their interferometric visibilities become separable, independently of the emission model, on three baseline ranges within 1.4--6.2 G$λ$ at errors of $\simeq36\,μ$Jy, and at $L_\star=2.64\,$G$λ$ at $\simeq71\,μ$Jy. This is about 28 times below the 2017 Event Horizon Telescope statistical uncertainty. We suggest that the widest detection window demands minutes-long coherent integrations, favoring a near-quantum-limited space interferometer.

candidates.title: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in a diamond nanocavity: demonstration and limits at the nanoscale
candidates.abstract: Diamond quantum sensors promise both high spatial resolution and high sensitivity; however, conventional photoluminescence-based spin readout can be difficult to integrate efficiently. Infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond provides a promising alternative, although the sensitivity of compact absorption-based sensors is limited by the short optical interaction length between the probe field and the NV ensemble. To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate, for the first time, singlet-absorption magnetometry using spin-dense diamond nanocavities. By probing cavity modes near the 1042 nm NV singlet transition, we observe spin-dependent cavity transmission and perform cavity-enhanced magnetic field sensing. We further develop and experimentally validate a model that accurately predicts the spin-dependent cavity response, describes the optimal operating conditions, and identifies the practical limitations of different optically detected magnetic resonance modalities. candidates.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
candidates.abstract: Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments. APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. candidates.title: Chiral Domain-Wall Modes in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Quantum dynamical systems driven by both unitary evolution and measurements open a new landscape of nonequilibrium phases of matter. The role of topology in enriching this landscape remains less understood than that of entanglement and symmetry. A particularly interesting question concerns protected dynamical modes localized on spacetime domain walls between topologically distinct dynamical phases. These dynamical topological domain-wall modes (DTDMs) are well understood only for $0+1$D walls in $1+1$D fermionic dynamics. In this work, we study $1+1$D topological domain walls in $2+1$D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics, modeled by topological adaptive circuits that steer the two sides of each wall toward a Chern insulator and a trivial insulator through measurements and feedforward corrections. Although the circuits target no particular wall state, each wall hosts $1+1$D chiral DTDMs. At long times in each quantum trajectory, they exhibit logarithmic scaling of entanglement and charge variance and algebraically decaying density correlations, surprisingly consistent with the ground state of a $1+1$D chiral free-fermion conformal field theory. candidates.title: Two Timescales of Forgetting in Fine-tuning of Language Models: Fast Behavioral Suppression and Slow Representational Drift
candidates.abstract: Today, a core pipeline of artificial intelligence systems is pretraining on a broad range of text corpora and then fine-tuning on specific tasks or desired behaviors. Yet we still have limited understanding of how fine-tuning on a restricted data distribution modifies representations acquired during pretraining. In particular, it remains unclear whether surface behavioral suppression happens together with the erasure of latent representations that support it. candidates.title: When precision exceeds fidelity: systematic error quantification for inference with misspecified simulators
candidates.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, accepted to Sim2Science: ML with Imperfect Scientific Models at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
candidates.abstract: As scientific datasets grow in complexity and precision, the primary source of uncertainty in parameter inference shifts from measurement noise to systematic errors within the simulators themselves. In this setting, Bayesian evidence concentrates on whichever misspecified model best approximates the data. Evidence-weighted model averaging can then underestimate systematic uncertainty when one model component compensates for the misspecification of another component. We posit that in this case, the key question is how each model responds to discrepancies between simulator and data. We show that the local response of an inferred parameter to perturbations in the data --- the model's influence map --- can be estimated efficiently from forward evaluations of the simulator at existing posterior samples. Propagating discrepancy residuals through these influence maps enables individual sources of systematic bias to be isolated. candidates.title: LatENSO v1.0: a learned latent state of the tropical Pacific for seasonal ENSO operators and forecasting
candidates.comment: 61 pages, 14 figures. Submitted to Geoscientific Model Development
candidates.abstract: Here we present LatENSO v1.0, a machine-learning forecast system for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) built around a learned, 32-dimensional state of the tropical Pacific. A Swin-transformer autoencoder compresses thirteen monthly-averaged ocean and atmosphere fields into 32 numbers, trained to reconstruct the fields, with no forecast target. The 32 numbers rebuild the fields as well as O(100) empirical orthogonal functions. Two seasonal operators use this state. The first is the extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO) with two directions of the learned state among its variables; we call it XRO-lat. The second is a Floquet modal operator (FMO) of three damped oscillators, which forecasts a correction added to a least-squares base forecast made from four observed predictors. We evaluate both against the recharge oscillator, XRO and a deep echo-state network (DESN), all refitted on identical data, cross-validation folds and verification windows (1981-2024). candidates.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
candidates.abstract: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

candidates.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
candidates.abstract: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.

candidates.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
candidates.abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

candidates.title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
candidates.comment: 40 pages+4 appendices, 14 figures, 13 tables, ancillary code included
candidates.abstract: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. candidates.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
candidates.abstract: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gröbner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators. An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

candidates.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
candidates.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in JPS Conference Proceedings (SCES2026)
candidates.abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 Å$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 Å$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

candidates.title: Formation of Electron Velocity Distribution Functions at low-\{beta} Quasi-Perpendicular Shocks From Physical-Mass-Ratio PIC Simulations
candidates.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
candidates.abstract: At low-\{beta} quasi-perpendicular shocks, the origins of upstream field-aligned electron beams and downstream flat-top distributions remain unresolved. Using 2D fully kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at the physical ion-to-electron mass ratio (mi/me = 1836), we found that the shock transition region is dominated by electromagnetic whistler-mode turbulence driven by the modified two-stream instability (MTSI) of reflected ions, not by the electrostatic instabilities as suggested by some previous studies using a reduced mass ratio. Beams in the upstream are produced mainly by shock-drift acceleration (SDA) at the ramp, whereas we attribute the downstream flat-top distributions to nonuniform acceleration by the parallel electric field. Electrons experience different field strengths, polarities, and interaction durations along their trajectories, leading to a spread of parallel velocity changes that broadens and flattens the distribution. These results highlight the importance of using the physical mass ratio in exploring the electron dynamics of low-\{beta} shocks.

candidates.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
candidates.abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. candidates.title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
candidates.comment: 7 main figures; Supplementary Information included (7 figures and 30 tables)
candidates.abstract: Classical dimensional analysis defines admissible dimensionless representations but does not determine which combinations capture the dominant physical dependence, whether it changes across physical regimes, or when dependent-variable rescaling is required. We present AI Buckingham, an agentic framework for autonomous dimensionless discovery from natural-language descriptions of physical problems and observational data. It couples reasoning and planning by a large language model (LLM) with predefined symbolic and numerical tools. Literature-based knowledge retrieval supports dimensional checking, gradient-based clustering identifies physical regimes, and mutual information provides an objective, reparameterization-invariant criterion for identifying dominant dimensionless groups. Explicit numerical criteria determine the group count and assess simplification. Across ten physical systems spanning fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, thermal convection and additive manufacturing, AI Buckingham recovers established similarity representations and resolves regime-dependent scalings. candidates.title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
candidates.abstract: In the two-dimensional (2D) Gross-Pitaevskii model for a Bose gas, the naive dimensional non-equilibrium wave-turbulence power-law prediction for the direct energy cascade coincides with thermal equilibrium and therefore carries no energy flux. We resolve this degeneracy by deriving a logarithmically corrected spectrum that supports a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales. A systematic asymptotic expansion of the wave-kinetic collision integral determines the logarithmic exponent to be 1/3, while the small-scale dissipation scale sets the upper cutoff in the logarithmic correction. Regularization of a marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale yields an estimate of the spectral prefactor for asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales. Simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic equations support the predicted spectral shape. Over finite spectral ranges, the correction produces apparent power laws steeper than the dimensional prediction, offering a possible explanation for the steep spectra observed in 2D Bose gas experiments. candidates.title: Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
candidates.abstract: Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification. A sparse-regression surrogate of the vector field is reconstructed from the data, and its Jacobian, estimated with a matrix-free Krylov method, is analysed with Computational Singular Perturbation diagnostics. The resulting fast-slow partition guides the learning of explicit SIM algebraic representations through regression, and the reduced model follows by restricting the dynamics to it. For a linear stochastic system, this regression agrees with the Mori-Zwanzig projection at leading order in the timescale ratio. candidates.abstract: At finite bond dimension $χ$, tensor network renormalization (TNR) of a critical model eventually becomes gapped. candidates.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
candidates.abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. To bridge classical AI and QML, we propose QPAT (QCBM-Prior-Assisted Training), a universal framework that employs a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) as a learnable generative prior to provide a task-aligned structured inductive bias during classical model training. The framework can be seamlessly integrated into any classical backbone, including LSTMs, CNNs, and Transformers. candidates.title: Existence of single-resonance parametric bound states in the continuum: System of Schrödinger equations
candidates.abstract: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is an eigenmode of a linear wave system with its eigen-frequency embedded in the radiation continuum of scattering states. At the frequency of a BIC, scattering problems with given incident waves from infinity lose uniqueness. Due to their close connection with strong resonance effects, BICs have found many useful applications in classical and quantum wave systems. Existence theories of BICs have been established for some cases involving the so-called symmetry-protected BICs, Friedrich-Wintgen BICs, and Fabry-Perot BICs. The single-resonance parametric BICs (srp-BICs) are another important class of BICs. Such a BIC emerges from a single resonant state through tuning a real parameter. Using a simple system of two one-dimensional Schrödinger equations, we demonstrate the formation of srp-BICs and establish a rigorous existence theory.

candidates.title: OrbACE: Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion
candidates.abstract: Accurate electronic-structure reference data are expensive, motivating interatomic potentials that learn effectively from limited training sets. We introduce OrbACE (Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion), a framework that supplements an E(3)-equivariant cluster-expansion backbone with inexpensive electronic-structure descriptors. On ANI-1x at the $ω$B97X/6-31G* level, its atom-centered variant, OrbACE-A, trained on 10,000 configurations and evaluated on 442,000 held-out configurations, achieves energy and force mean absolute errors of 3.16 meV/atom and 76 meV/angstrom in direct learning, compared with 9.61 meV/atom and 146 meV/angstrom for MACE with matched backbone settings. This reduces the energy error by a factor of three and approximately halves the force error. Its energy error is also below that of the best delta-corrected MACE baseline, 5.00 meV/atom, although its force error is slightly higher. Combining OrbACE-A with a Hartree-Fock delta baseline further reduces the errors to 1.48 meV/atom and 35 meV/angstrom. candidates.title: Using waveform types, discrete Sobolev distances, and trend compatibility to cluster short time series of clinical data
candidates.abstract: Clinical tests, such as the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), perturb a physiological system at rest and record its excursion over a fixed protocol window as a short, undersampled time series. Such curves rarely allow parameter identification at the individual level, yet their trends carry physiological information that emerges at the population level as recurrent response patterns. Standard clustering methods aggregate differences globally and average out those trends, losing precisely the information about how the system regains control after the perturbation; identifying response patterns requires a method that preserves them. We present a nonparametric framework that factorizes each curve into unit waveforms, sorts them with a symbolic trend-compatibility filter, and compares compatible shapes using discrete Sobolev-type distances on finite differences up to order $k$. The number of clusters, i.e., distinct response types, equals the number of realizable trend patterns the cohort populates, validated by resampling. Applied to 1283 five-point OGTTs, the method identifies 7 glycemia and 8 insulinemia types. The count holds across a threefold range of resolution. In benchmarks a

candidates.title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
candidates.comment: 28 pages, 1 figure; general treatment of the Dirac equation (in the absence of torsion) for cases in which $γ^{\hat 0}$ serves as the hermitizing matrix for the Dirac matrices
candidates.abstract: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. candidates.title: Differential coupling drives Turing pattern formation in neural fields: a mechanism for Parkinson's disease and deep brain stimulation
candidates.comment: main: 14 pages, 6 figures; SM: 13 pages, 10 figures
candidates.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an effective treatment for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Abnormal beta-band synchronization in the basal ganglia and thalamocortical circuit is a hallmark of PD, but a theoretical framework linking network synchronization to spatial pattern formation is lacking. Here we show that a two-layer neural field model with differential interlayer coupling undergoes a Turing instability, spontaneously generating a diverse repertoire of spatially ordered patterns, including stripes, spots, rings, and spiral waves. The model yields the critical conditions and wavelengths for this instability, quantitatively predicting the observed pattern morphologies. Crucially, the interlayer difference, a natural measure of synchrony, exhibits strongly regime dependent dynamics. These findings establish a dynamical framework linking spatial pattern formation to pathological beta-band synchronization, providing a theoretical mechanism for DBS modulation of network states and a mathematical basis for optimizing stimulation parameters.

candidates.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
candidates.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achiev

candidates.title: Symmetry-Aware Residual Learning of Few-Body Molecular Wave Functions
candidates.comment: 32 pages, 15 figures. Meital Bojan and Mikhail Maslov contributed equally to this work
candidates.abstract: Ultracold polar molecules are a highly controllable platform for engineering quantum matter, but modeling their few-body properties remains computationally challenging. Their anisotropic long-range interactions and rich internal structure lead to high-dimensional eigenvalue problems for which conventional grid-based solvers are largely restricted to two-molecule systems. To address this limitation, we introduce a physics-informed neural variational method that exploits known physical structure of the molecular wave function. Our key idea is to factor the wave function into analytic and neural components. The analytic component encodes rotational symmetry and asymptotic decay, while the neural residual learns the remaining intermediate-range behavior. This decomposition reduces the effective dimensionality of the problem without relying on ad hoc approximations or problem-specific discretization grids. We benchmark our method against high-accuracy two-molecule solvers and recover both ground and excited bound states with mean relative errors below 0.01%. candidates.title: Machine-Learning Spin-Fermion Models for Strongly Disordered Magnets: Sb-Doped MnTe
candidates.abstract: Metallic altermagnets are promising for spintronics, but most altermagnets are insulating. Doping can induce metallicity, but introduces chemical and magnetic disorder that is challenging to model from first principles. Here, we introduce a machine-learning approach that renormalizes first-principles calculations onto disordered spin-fermion models. The learned models accurately reproduce first-principles magnetic and electronic properties and enable predictions of millions of inequivalent long-range exchange couplings in large disordered supercells. Applied to Sb-doped MnTe, the approach shows that altermagnetism persists up to about 25\% Sb, and reveals disorder broadening as a new factor controlling spin selectivity. More broadly, our work opens a route to combining renormalization with machine-learned Hamiltonians for strongly disordered materials.

candidates.title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
candidates.abstract: Without data, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in continuous time have so far failed to develop vortex shedding past a circular cylinder in a domain symmetric about the wake centerline: the training converges to the steady symmetric solution. We obtain shedding at Re=100 with a continuous-time PINN trained over successive time windows, without any reference data and without temporal discretization, the symmetry being broken by an analytical, divergence-free initial condition. The Strouhal number and the mean drag coefficient agree with an OpenFOAM solution computed on the same domain to within 0.5%. The pressure, however, is discontinuous at the junctions between windows, and the lift coefficient is a staircase. We relate this discontinuity to the differential-algebraic structure of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, of index 2 after spatial discretization: a consistent initial condition of each window must satisfy the constraint $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ for the velocity, and the hidden constraint $\nabla\cdot\partial_t\mathbf{v}=0$, with $\partial_t\mathbf{v}$ given by the momentum equation, then determines the pressure. candidates.title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
candidates.abstract: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state. This is formulated in an autonomous system framework, which can be obtained via a compactification of time. Techniques from singular perturbation theory elucidate how canard trajectories shape the geometric structure of the quasithreshold as the system's pullback attractor moves through it. The probability with which weakly stochastically driven sample paths travel through the quasithreshold and undertake (i) solely noise-induced and (ii) combined rate- and noise-induced excitations is estimated numerically for each of the corresponding forcing scenarios, using the adaptive multilevel splitting algorithm. candidates.title: Gaussian priors from nonlinear PDEs with the semiclassical approximation
candidates.abstract: Probabilistic numerical methods for partial differential equations (PDE) combines the governing physics with observations to treat solving the PDE as a Bayesian inverse problem. This allows techniques to quantify the uncertainty in the field reconstruction under model-form error. In the majority of cases, a Gaussian prior is assigned to the field of interest, and Bayes's theorem in the infinite-dimensional setting is used to derive the posterior. While Gaussians have been shown to be well-suited for linear PDEs, a similar treatment for nonlinear PDEs remains open-ended. In this work, study the use of the semiclassical approximation to construct Gaussian priors from variational energies or integrated square residuals for probabilistic numerics. The prior is derived by expanding the PDE energy about a stable solution and uncovering a Gaussian form. We then analyze the different characteristics of the resulting priors as they pertain to the inverse problem. In particular, we find that the covariance operator is given by the inverse of the Hessian of the energy whose associated Cameron-Martin space is the solution space of the PDE. candidates.title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
candidates.abstract: Earth's thermohaline ocean circulation may support multiple equilibria and abrupt transitions. Similar bifurcation structures for different ocean models suggest common underlying dynamics across the model hierarchy. Here we propose a unifying framework from tracer conservation, in which surface fluxes are balanced by dissipative and advective tracer transport. We express this flux balance through a large-scale tracer gradient and a transport efficiency that measures how strongly circulation displaces the tracer field from its no-flow "conductive" state. The flux balance quantifies the transport contributions that sustain each circulation state and give rise to abrupt transitions. In a three-dimensional ocean-basin model, we find nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold and linear dissipation dominates the recovery threshold. Temperature has additional dissipation from surface restoring, making thermal fluxes more dissipation-dominated than salinity fluxes. The tracer contrasts and boundary layers that a given circulation generates produce distinct transport regimes, approximately quadratic in circulation strength for weak flow and linear for strong flow. candidates.title: Toward Automated Strong-Lens Modeling with Agentic Workflows: An Application to Euclid Q1 Lenses
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. The lens-model catalog and diagnostic plots are available at https://github.com/caoxiaoyue/lens-orchestra. The full codebase will be released upon acceptance
candidates.abstract: Ongoing and forthcoming wide-field surveys will discover $O(10^5)$ galaxy-galaxy strong lenses, shifting the main bottleneck from detection to reliable physical modeling. Conventional forward-modeling pipelines still rely on case-by-case expert judgment and manual tuning to mask contaminants, initialize priors, diagnose unphysical fits, and reconfigure failed runs. We present Lens-Orchestra, an automated workflow coupling a team of multimodal large language model agents to multi-stage physical modeling with elliptical power-law mass profiles, external shear, and pixelized source reconstructions. Launched via natural-language instructions, it modeled 185 Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) grade-A lens candidates with published mass models without human intervention, completing 149 fits. Independent human evaluation confirmed 140 usable models, including 126 grade-I fits with noise-level residuals (with only 6.0% of completed fits unacceptable), and endorsed all 36 halted runs. candidates.title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$
candidates.abstract: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level $k\geq 3$. Global $SU(2)$ symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level $k+1$, built from the currents on its two sides. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for $k=3$ and $5$, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.

candidates.title: Do Not Let the Prior Heal the Anomaly: Selective Anchoring for Detection from Incomplete Measurements
candidates.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures, 23 tables. Includes supplementary material
candidates.abstract: Generative priors can recover anatomical detail from incomplete medical measurements, but may erase the very lesions that imaging aims to detect, even when the measurements contain evidence of them. We introduce selective anchoring that protects reliably measured image components from prior-driven changes, while allowing expressive generative models to reconstruct unresolved structure. Acquisition uncertainty in the protected components is either added deterministically to the downstream test or carried by the ensemble through stochastic perturbations of the readings. We implement this principle as a wrapper for pretrained diffusion and flow samplers and as AnchoredFM, a fast constrained flow model. Under a linear-Gaussian measurement model, the protected coefficients are unbiased in expectation and achieve nominal interval coverage across repeated acquisitions, independently of the learned prior. Across sparse-view CT, accelerated brain MRI, and photoacoustic tomography, selective anchoring improves lesion contrast preservation and uncertainty reliability, and can reduce reconstruction error within lesions. candidates.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
candidates.comment: Main text 12 pages, 8 figures, and appendices. Comments are welcome. Code available at github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent
candidates.abstract: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results. These examples also show its ability to search the literature, analyze non-power-law spectra using user-provided model code, and develop new analysis functions, such as signal-injection simulations. \system is also a powerful tool for improving and testing existing analysis code, as we dem

candidates.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
candidates.abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.

candidates.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
candidates.comment: 66 pages + appendices, 19 figures, 1 table; comments and references are welcome
candidates.abstract: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. candidates.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
candidates.abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

candidates.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
candidates.abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy $Δ>1$, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point $Δ=1$, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For $Δ>1$, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. candidates.title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
candidates.abstract: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

candidates.title: Sharp one-shot bounds and optimal exponents of universal randomness extraction
candidates.abstract: We introduce techniques for the study of randomness extraction against quantum side information (privacy amplification) by relating this problem to variants of hypothesis testing tasks with quadratic constraints. Building also on the recently introduced measured smooth entropy approach of [Regula and Tomamichel, arXiv:2603.04493], we precisely determine the optimal scaling of the error of quantum privacy amplification in several regimes. Our results apply to the standard operational security criterion based on trace distance and focus in particular on universal classes of hash functions. On the technical side, our investigation reveals connections with operator space theory methods used in non-commutative Khintchine inequalities. As one application, we give a one-shot converse bound that shows the leftover hash lemma of [arXiv:2603.04493] to be tight up to a constant factor for all strongly 4-universal hash functions. This allows us to evaluate the asymptotic i.i.d. error exponent of universal randomness extraction for all rates, matching the bound of [Dupuis, arXiv:2105.05342] and improving also earlier classical asymptotic results of [Hayashi, arXiv:1010.1358]. candidates.title: Magnetization, susceptibility, and entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped homometallic tetranuclear and pentanuclear Cu(II) complexes
candidates.abstract: We present a theoretical investigation of the magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and quantum entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped tetranuclear ($Cu_4$) and pentanuclear ($Cu_5$) Cu(II) clusters, motivated by experimentally realized molecular spin systems. In both cases, the study presents a discussion of the comparison between experimental data and theoretical analytical calculations of magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature. The correlation between magnetization jumps and magnetic susceptibility peaks, along with the presence of entanglement entropy plateaus as a function of external magnetic fields, is analyzed in the low-temperature regime. Overall, the results demonstrate that the cluster size, geometry, and interaction anisotropy play a crucial role in shaping both the thermodynamic and the entanglement properties. In addition, the study is based on antiferromagnetic Heisenberg spin Hamiltonians, with the inclusion of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

candidates.title: Hidden f-wave TIVC and Quantum Phase Transitions in Metallic States of Twisted Bilayer Graphene
candidates.abstract: We study the ground state phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at magic angle as function of carrier density and the Coulomb interaction. The carrier density is varied between the fillings $ν=-2$ and $ν=-3$ and the Coulomb interaction is tuned by changing the gate distance. Our results reveal that the well established Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) phase near $ν=-2$, contains a hidden $f$-wave time-reversal symmetric intervalley coherent (TIVC) order, whose strength gradually increases within the metallic regime of the intervalley coherent (IVC) phase away from $ν=-2$. This finding is interesting in the light of a recent experimental work [26], where the signatures of the TIVC phase has been reported in ultra-clean samples. We further show that the system goes through multiple phase transitions as the carrier density is tuned. Near the $ν=-2$, the IVC phase is the ground state, which gives way to valley polarized phase through a second-order-like phase transition as the carrier density is lowered. candidates.title: Geometry, masking and selection in Differential Evolution and SOMA on quantum state manifolds
candidates.comment: Submitted to Swarm and Evolutionary Computation for publication
candidates.abstract: Differential Evolution (DE) and the Self-Organizing Migrating Algorithm (SOMA) generate new candidates through vector arithmetic: they subtract population members, scale the difference, and mask coordinates. Many practical search spaces are not vector spaces, however. Rotation angles are periodic, normalized states lie on spheres and projective spaces, and circuit parameters are coupled through the quantum states they produce. We present a systematic study of how such geometry affects the core operations of DE and SOMA. Keeping the operators and selection rules fixed, we replace only their geometric primitives and separate the effects of difference construction, masking, and selection in a large paired numerical study covering textbook manifolds and variational quantum problems. Geometry-consistent differences make full-crossover (CR = 1) DE significantly better on 16 of 31 non-Euclidean configurations, with no significant deterioration, and the advantage persists when the measured computational cost of each variant is taken into account. candidates.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.

candidates.title: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine
candidates.abstract: Mapping optimization problems to the restricted coefficient range of an 8-bit CIM can distort their encoded energy landscapes. We investigate whether three coefficient-range mitigation techniques previously studied for quantum annealing---interaction extension, bounded-coefficient encoding, and augmented Lagrangian penalties---improve end-to-end optimization outcomes. Experiments on weighted Max-Cut, multidimensional knapsack, and quadratic assignment show that the benefits are selective. At a fixed number of CIM calls, intermediate interaction extension yields higher mean best Max-Cut objectives, whereas aggressive extension degrades performance. Bounded-coefficient encoding improves the mean best feasible profit on one knapsack instance but not the other. Augmented Lagrangian perturbations increase feasibility when unshifted constraint penalties are too weak, but do not outperform the best unshifted penalty setting. Overall, coefficient-range mitigation is most effective when its strength is tuned to the problem and encoding, with aggressive mitigation potentially offsetting its benefits.

candidates.title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
candidates.comment: XX pages, 12 figures in the main text; Supplementary Material included
candidates.abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). candidates.title: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents
candidates.abstract: Amine-impregnated sorbents with the highest nominal CO2 capacity are frequently the least deployable, as amine beyond the pore-volume limit blocks active sites. Yet multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) for direct air capture (DAC) treats formulation search as unconstrained. We encode the pore-filling boundary as an explicit outcome constraint, c(x) = tanh(1 - phi_hat) - tau, and use it as a diagnostic instrument on a hand-curated, DOI-traceable benchmark of 618 solid-amine formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained MOBO attains higher nominal capacity (3.639 +/- 0.815 vs. 2.964 +/- 0.728 mmol/g, p = 1.0e-11), but across 100 seeds 63.2% of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary versus 39.3% under the constraint: it is rewarded for proposing candidates outside the pore-confined design regime. The constraint steers the front to lower loadings (55.8 vs. 65.2 wt%) and larger pores. The boundary is corroborated once apparatus effects are harmonized hierarchically: 77.8% of kinetic variance is between-laboratory, and pore filling carries a significant kinetic penalty (p = 0.002). candidates.title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
candidates.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
candidates.abstract: Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921. Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253. Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007, [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 or [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data. Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$λ$$λ$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$λ$$λ$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR.

candidates.title: Characterization and empirical correction of a spatially coherent spectral artifact in Gemini/GMOS-N IFU observations
candidates.abstract: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. candidates.title: Quantum Metric Connects Bond Delocalization to Phonon Softening
candidates.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures in main text. 14 pages, 1 figure in supplemental material
candidates.abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

candidates.title: Tunable quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect in the PT-symmetric sliding antiferroelectric MoS$_2$
candidates.abstract: The quantum metric, the real part of a quantum geometric tensor, plays an important role in fundamental transport and optical responses of quantum materials. While net quantum metric effects are typically realized by breaking both time-reversal (T) and inversion (P) symmetries, valley-contrast mechanisms enable the probing of quantum geometry in centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic systems, revealing physical signatures beyond Berry curvature. Here, we design a four-layer MoS$_2$ platform that combines sliding antiferroelectric order with strain-induced $C_{3z}$ breaking to realize a quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect (NVHE) under preserved P and T symmetries. Reversible interlayer sliding (ABBA $\leftrightarrow$ BAAB) provides nonvolatile electrical control of the valley response. First-principles calculations reveal an outer-layer-dominated NVHE with tunable sign and magnitude. This symmetry-preserving, sliding-tunable strategy activates hidden quantum geometric phenomena in realistic two-dimensional materials and opens a clean pathway for tunable valleytronics and quantum information devices.

candidates.title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
candidates.abstract: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. candidates.title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
candidates.abstract: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. candidates.title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
candidates.abstract: We present a Cartesian staggered-grid large-eddy simulation framework for modelling coastal ocean waves using the Dopamine solver. The framework combines a geometric volume-of-fluid method for simulating free-surface wave evolution with one-way-coupled Lagrangian point-particle tracking for heavy and buoyant particles. A ghost-cell immersed-boundary method represents stationary solid boundaries, including the seabed and coastal obstacles, and their interaction with free-surface waves. The framework includes the Vreman and anisotropic minimum-dissipation (AMD) sub-grid-scale models for simulating near-wall turbulence. Comparisons with analytical solutions and established experimental and numerical benchmarks illustrate the framework's ability to reproduce wave dynamics and particle motion. The results provide promising insights into the framework's capabilities for coastal ocean modelling applications focused on investigating small-scale turbulent physics using a low-numerical-dissipation approach. candidates.title: UNIONS and Euclid: Calibrating point source-galaxy separation for ground-based surveys
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. Some material is available online on https://github.com/GFThomas/StarGal_ground_Euclid
candidates.abstract: Efficient separation of unresolved point sources from extended objects (star-galaxy separation) is essential for deep wide-field imaging surveys, particularly at faint magnitudes where morphological differences become subtle. We assess two morphology-based classification methods applied to single-band, ground-based imaging from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS), using Euclid observations as a high-fidelity reference to evaluate their performance and to train one of the methods. We analysed 8 deg$^2$ of overlapping UNIONS $r$-band and Euclid $I_E$ data, comprising more than $7\times10^{5}$ sources. The Euclid data enable robust morphological labelling down to $I_E\simeq 26$, which we used to train and validate two classification approaches applied to UNIONS alone: a curve-of-growth method and a supervised neural-network classifier, both based on aperture photometry and image-quality information. The curve-of-growth method yields an almost perfectly complete point-source sample ($>95\%$), but its purity decreases rapidly at $r \simeq 22.5$. candidates.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
candidates.abstract: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

candidates.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
candidates.abstract: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement.
