candidates.title: Ratio of $\barΛ$ to $K_\rm{S}^0$ production cross-sections in $pp$ collisions at 13.6TeV
candidates.comment: All figures and tables, along with machine-readable versions and any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lhcb-glance.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/6198/
candidates.abstract: The production cross-section ratio of promptly produced $\barΛ$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ hadrons is measured in proton-proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6TeV recorded in 2024 with the upgraded LHCb detector and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $64\rm{pb}^{-1}$. The ratio is presented as a function of transverse momentum, $p_\rm{T}$, and rapidity, $y$, in the ranges $0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\rm{GeV}/c$ and $2.0 < y < 4.5$. The results are in good agreement with previous measurements at different centre-of-mass energies. They are compared to predictions from currently available event generators and can be used as input in future event generator tunings.

candidates.title: Bar Kinematics in Paired and Isolated Galaxies: Slow Bars Are More Likely Found in Paired Galaxies
candidates.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
candidates.abstract: Bars are common structures in disk galaxies that can strongly influence the evolution of their hosts. Simulations predict that bars formed through tidal interactions tend to rotate slower than bars formed in isolation. We test this prediction observationally by studying the kinematics of 314 bars in galaxies between $0.016<z<0.130$. We use estimates of the bar pattern speed ($Ω_p$) and the rotation rate ($\mathcal{R}$) obtained from four studies using IFU data from the MaNGA survey. We cross-match the host galaxies of the bars to the Galaxy Zoo DESI catalogue in order to study their environment and classify each galaxy as paired or isolated. We find that bars that are slower in terms of $\mathcal{R}$ are more likely to be found in paired galaxies. The fraction of bars in paired galaxies increases from $5^{+6}_{-2}\%$ for $0<\mathcal{R}<1.0$ to $31^{+15}_{-9}\%$ for $3.0<\mathcal{R}<4.0$. candidates.title: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
candidates.abstract: Quantum reflection is a counter-intuitive process occurring when an atom is reflected by a rapidly-varying attraction towards a surface, for example the Casimir-Polder force. The reflection probability depends on the attractive potential and on the mass of the atom. For hydrogen isotopes, the potentials are nearly identical whereas significant differences in quantum reflection come from the effect of atomic mass. We calculate the quantum reflection probability for the three isotopes H, D or T falling onto the plane surface of an intrinsic silicon bulk. We show that the results obey scaling laws determined by scattering lengths calculated from theory. Moreover the scattering lengths also obey scaling laws with respect to atomic masses of the isotopes.

candidates.title: Length-scales and fractal scaling in dairy gels: comparisons of the insights from ultra-small angle neutron scattering and rheology
candidates.abstract: A key structural parameter that dictates the textural properties of a particulate gel is the fractal dimension (Df) of the network indicating self-similarity within the spatial range defined by the correlation length (xi). In this study dairy gels are formed from reconstituted skim milk at defined CM volume fractions via two different mechanisms: acidification, and enzymatic (rennet)-induction. Oscillatory rheology is performed to obtain the gelation times, the time-scale for the maturation of mechanical properties of the gel, and the viscoelastic properties of the gel. A direct probe of gel structure is ultra-small-angle neutron scattering (USANS) examining length-scales from approximately 60 nm up to 15 microns. Structural information is extracted from USANS of matured gels by comparing the measured differential scattering cross-section with that calculated from a model constrained by the sample composition. candidates.title: High-Precision Photometry with a scientific CMOS Camera: III Lab and on-Sky testing of Andor Toran-26B
candidates.abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras are increasingly used in modern astronomy, offering CCD-like performance with lower power use, faster readout, and reduced cost. candidates.title: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model
candidates.abstract: Within the standard prepare-measure framework, it has been demonstrated that certain compositions of two elementary quantum systems can produce beyond-quantum correlations and can even lead to perfect discrimination of two non-orthogonal quantum states. candidates.title: Bringing Singles to $GW$: A Coupled-Cluster Perspective on Orbital Relaxation
candidates.abstract: The one-shot $G_0W_0$ approximation suffers from a pronounced dependence on the underlying mean-field starting point. Here, we explore an alternative to conventional self-consistent $GW$ schemes by introducing single excitations within the recently established connection between $GW$ and extended coupled-cluster (ECC) theory. candidates.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
candidates.abstract: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

candidates.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): the fraction of radio-detected quasi-stellar objects at high redshift
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
candidates.abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) to assess the fraction of high-z quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) that are radio-emitting at ~0.2 mJy/beam level and to establish if the radio emission is mainly produced by relativistic jets. In total, 124 high-z QSOs are detected by EMU, corresponding to 15% of the sample. The large majority (70%) of the QSOs radio detected by EMU are reported in the radio for the first time. We use this sample to establish the detection rate at different optical magnitudes. candidates.abstract: Metasurfaces are increasingly employed for sophisticated polarization transformations, including general unitary and nonunitary Jones operations. Despite substantial advances in analytical synthesis methods, inverse design of these transformations remains challenging. Here, we show that the particular mathematical structure of Jones polarization transformations makes optimal effective-susceptibility synthesis analytically tractable within the generalized sheet transition condition (GSTC) framework. For reciprocal, lossless dipolar metasurfaces, we establish exact feasibility and global minimum attainment, and derive sharp effective-susceptibility bounds for representative unitary and nonunitary transformations. We identify when magnetoelectric coupling lowers the minimum susceptibility, when it offers no resource advantage, and how the required material response depends on the prescribed polarization transformation. Applications to polarization rotations, tunable compensators, and polarization-state separation, including unambiguous discrimination, demonstrate sharp physical limits and material-resource trade-offs.
